## Contract summarizer series

A serverless reader that takes a long contract and hands back a one-page plain-English summary — who, what, money, key dates, and the renewal or cancellation terms — then flags the clauses worth a closer look, like auto-renewal, penalties, and liability. Every point cites the exact clause it came from, and it never gives legal advice; it points a busy owner at what matters and says when to call a lawyer.

- [A contract summarizer on AWS for a few dollars a month](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/contract-summarizer-on-aws/): The whole system on one page — an intake, a reader, and a delivery piece — plus the read, pull-terms, flag-risks flow every contract runs through, all grounded in the actual clause text.
- [How a contract gets read](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-a-contract-gets-read/): Three lanes feed one reader — a Drive folder you drop files into, an inbox-forwarding lane, and an e-sign webhook — then Textract reads the pages and a Python pass splits them into numbered clauses.
- [How the key terms get pulled](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-the-key-terms-get-pulled/): A single cheap Haiku 4.5 call fills a fixed shape — parties, deal, money, key dates, renewal and cancellation — and every field must cite the clause it came from, or it is left blank rather than guessed.
- [How risky clauses get flagged](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-risky-clauses-get-flagged/): Retrieval over the contract's own clauses finds the few worth a second look — auto-renewal, penalties, liability, exclusivity — and Sonnet 4.6 explains each in plain words, never as legal advice, flagging when to call a lawyer.
- [How a summary stays grounded](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-a-summary-stays-grounded/): Every claim is checked against the real clause text before the one-page summary goes out, the not-legal-advice banner is attached, and a person approves it before it is filed and delivered as a Doc and an email.
- [What the contract summarizer costs](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/what-the-contract-summarizer-costs/): A few dollars a month at SMB volume. The cost is mostly reading each contract once — Textract plus a cheap Haiku pass — with Sonnet firing only on the handful of flagged clauses.
- [Engineering reference: the contract summarizer architecture](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/contract-summarizer-engineering-reference/): Same system, drawn for engineers — region, service names, Bedrock model IDs, the S3 Vectors clause index, Lambda inventory, IAM scopes, the SES inbound rule set, and the DynamoDB schemas.

- [How a receipt gets read](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-a-receipt-gets-read/): Textract reads the vendor, date, total, and tax with a confidence score each; the reader checks the threshold, looks for duplicates, and picks one of four results: filed, needs-review, duplicate, or rejected.

- [How the responder picks a move](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-the-responder-picks-a-move/): Four moves, one pick per review — auto-reply, draft, escalate, ignore. Safety keywords bypass everything; named staff and specifics become drafts.
- [How a reply stays in your voice](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-a-reply-stays-in-your-voice/): Three Drive docs ground the composer; four guardrails sit between the model and the post button — citation, no PII echo, no fabricated specifics, no off-policy promises.
- [What the review responder costs](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/what-the-review-responder-costs/): A coffee a month at SMB review volume. Pennies per review, dominated by Bedrock tokens.
- [Engineering reference: the review responder architecture](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/review-responder-engineering-reference/): The same system drawn for engineers — service names, resource identifiers, region, Bedrock model IDs, Knowledge Base wiring, Google Business Profile and Meta Graph API specifics.

## Website chat assistant series

A serverless chat widget for a small business website on AWS — answers visitors from your own knowledge in real time, hands the rest to a human cleanly, and turns every miss into a better answer next week. A few dollars a month at SMB volume.

- [A website chat assistant on AWS for a few dollars a month](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/website-chat-assistant-on-aws/): A small chat widget that answers visitors from your own knowledge in real time, hands the rest cleanly. The whole system on one page.
- [How a conversation starts and stays alive](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-a-conversation-starts/): Connect, exchange, idle. A websocket and a small scratchpad — short-term memory only, no long-lived profile.
- [How the assistant answers](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-the-assistant-answers/): Search first, then generate. Four tools, one pick per turn — answer, clarify, hand off, decline. No citation, no auto-answer.
- [How a handoff to a human works](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-a-handoff-to-a-human-works/): Tell, package, deliver, hold. The visitor never repeats themselves; the transcript is the ticket.
- [How gaps become better answers](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-gaps-become-better-answers/): A clockwise loop — log every miss, group similar questions, write a paragraph, re-index automatically. Ten minutes a week.
- [What the chat assistant costs](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/what-the-chat-assistant-costs/): A coffee a month at SMB volume. Cents per conversation, dominated by Bedrock tokens.
- [Engineering reference: the chat assistant architecture](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/website-chat-assistant-engineering-reference/): The same system drawn for engineers — service names, resource identifiers, region, Bedrock model IDs, Knowledge Base wiring.

## Booking assistant series

A serverless booking assistant on AWS — reads appointment requests from a web form or email, queries Google Calendar for availability, applies your service rules, proposes slots, and atomically confirms the customer's pick. A few dollars a month at SMB volume.

- [A booking assistant on AWS for a few dollars a month](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/booking-assistant-on-aws/): Reads appointment requests, checks Google Calendar, proposes slots that respect your service rules, locks in the customer's pick. The whole system on one page.
- [How a booking request reaches the assistant](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-a-booking-request-reaches-the-assistant/): Three lanes at the door — web-form fast path, AI-handle for free-text email, direct escalate for VIPs.
- [How the assistant understands the request](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-the-assistant-understands-the-request/): Three small extractors run in parallel — service, time window, contact. Confidence on every field; borderline becomes a draft.
- [How the assistant picks slots](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-the-assistant-picks-slots/): Five filters in order — calendar query, working hours, duration plus buffers, blackouts and capacity, then rank.
- [How a booking gets confirmed](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-a-booking-gets-confirmed/): Claim, write, confirm, remind — in that order. An atomic claim row prevents double-booking even under concurrent clicks.
- [What the booking assistant costs](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/what-the-booking-assistant-costs/): A coffee a month at SMB volume. Cents per request; the web-form lane is essentially free.
- [Engineering reference: the booking assistant architecture](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/booking-assistant-engineering-reference/): The same system drawn for engineers — service names, resource identifiers, region, Bedrock model IDs, Google Calendar API choices.

## Document pipeline series

A serverless document pipeline that reads documents, validates each one, and sends structured data straight to wherever it needs to go. A few dollars a month.

- [A document pipeline on AWS for a few dollars a month](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/document-pipeline-on-aws/): Reads documents for you, checks each one, sends structured data to wherever it needs to go.
- [How a document enters the pipeline](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-a-document-enters-the-pipeline/): Three ways in — uploaded, emailed, or dropped. Screened for trouble before any AI runs.
- [How the AI reads a document](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-the-ai-reads-a-document/): Two AIs in sequence — a specialist for layout, a generalist for meaning. The combo is more accurate than either alone.
- [How extraction stays accurate](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-extraction-stays-accurate/): The validator gates obvious cases through and queues the unsure ones for a 5-second human review.
- [How the data flows out](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/how-the-data-flows-out/): Each destination is a small pluggable piece. The rules file decides which document type lands in which tool.
- [What the document pipeline costs](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/what-the-document-pipeline-costs/): A coffee a month at typical SMB volume. Cents per document, not dollars.
- [Engineering reference: the document pipeline architecture](https://www.allanninal.dev/build/document-pipeline-engineering-reference/): The same system drawn for engineers — service names, resource identifiers, region, Bedrock model IDs.
